caption: Researchers' papers against AI agent systems on the inquiry graph (graph v0.4.2). Papers are the 374 of 525 eligible round-1 papers (2022) with full text and a valid coding (379 were coded; the sample is set by full-text access, not drawn at random), coded by Claude Opus 5.5 under codebook 1.5.0. Agent systems are 31 published AI agent systems hand-picked for a comparison talk (science agents, general agent patterns, multi-agent, coding and deep-research systems), coded from their papers and documentation, not from executed runs, by two model coders that did not see each other's work, a Claude Opus run (opus-b) and a Claude Sonnet run (sonnet-c), under loop codebook 0.1.2, which differs from the paper codebook; an agent loop is the cycle of steps the system repeats. (a) Share of papers whose coded final-paper workflow uses each node at least once (blue) and share of agent systems whose loops run it (orange; a node counts when marked full, and the share is the mean of the two coders). Nodes in graph order. Horizontal lines in (a) and (b) are 95% percentile bootstrap intervals (2000 resamples of papers or of agent systems, seed 2026); the intervals for K among papers (100%, [100, 100]) and P among agent systems (0%, [0, 0]) have zero width and are not visible. The four largest gaps, papers minus agent systems, are at Q question (98% of papers against 10% of agent systems), V vary or replicate (98% of papers against 10% of agent systems), I infer (84% of papers against 5% of agent systems), H hypothesize (84% of papers against 6% of agent systems); only R (68% of agent systems against 55% of papers) has the higher estimate among agent systems, with overlapping intervals. (b) Distinct nodes per workflow, median [95% interval]: papers 10 [10, 11], agent systems 3.5 [2, 4.5] (coder mean per system, hence half values). (c) Of the 55 researcher transitions (consecutive distinct nodes) found in at least 10% of papers, the number run in any loop of the 31 agent systems, per coder (opus-b: 31, sonnet-c: 23); the three most common transitions no loop runs are listed. Agent transitions are read from the coded loop step sequences, including steps on nodes not marked full (93 of 311 loop steps for opus-b, 81 of 197 loop steps for sonnet-c), so (c) counts more agent nodes than (a). Aggregated with the functions of tools/roadmap/g14_papers_vs_agents.py; inputs in the provenance fields of this file. Round 2 papers (open blue circles, n = 198) were computed here from the r2 codings with the g14 rules against the same agent codings.
